findings.text: Early boot uses a compact packed record holding a sixteen bit table bound plus a thirty two bit linear address for legacy descriptor table loading.
The SMAP signature constant equals 0x534D4150 corresponding to ASCII letters S M A P.

Boot formatting option bits occupy distinct powers of two: zero padding one, signed handling two, explicit plus four, blank for plus eight, left alignment sixteen, small case thirty two with fixed hex twenty requirement supporting case folding, alternate form sixty four.

Host string generator emits a C character array mapping capability word and bit positions to feature names, guarding each present name by a build time required mask test except the final table slot which is emitted unconditionally and absorbs the compiler terminator.

Text screen preservation assumes mode parameters were captured beforehand. Capture records column count, row count and cursor origin, then retains a copy of visible character cells only when heap space for the frame plus spare exists. Restoration does nothing for graphical video or when no snapshot exists, otherwise adapts the snapshot to current geometry with blank fill and clamps the remembered cursor inside visible bounds before requesting firmware repositioning and refreshing stored cursor state.

Thirty two bit firmware handover builds a new descriptor table from a stack copy of the firmware table extended with a sixty four bit code entry, records mixed mode operation, prepares an indirect far helper for later returns to firmware bitness, establishes identity large page coverage and a small hierarchy for continued execution, enables long mode and then far transfers to the common sixty four bit stub with firmware supplied arguments remapped.

Mixed mode firmware invocation bridges sixty four bit calling convention to thirty two bit convention, temporarily leaves paging and long mode to run the firmware target, preserves its result across mode restoration which keeps interrupts disabled, then cleans stack arguments and far returns.

Long mode activation in this early path always enables physical address extension, then extended feature long mode enable, then suppresses interrupts because firmware vectors are unsafe in the new mode, and finally enables paging.

Three externally reachable EFI entries exist: a thirty two bit stub that zeroes uninitialized storage and forwards the boot parameter pointer to common startup, a portable executable entry that only proceeds when extended processor features report long mode support and otherwise reports unsupported, and a sixty four bit stub that directly forwards to the handover entry.
Early exception handling reserves page aligned storage for exactly the architectural count of exception vectors.

Sixty four bit early setup loads a statically provided global descriptor table and refreshes data segments to the kernel data selector, optionally selects a virtualization communication handler when encrypted memory builds are active, and loads an interrupt table that contains only that optional entry before enabling descriptor use.

Paging level toggle code runs from a relocatable template that safeguards full width callee preserved state and the upper half of the stack pointer, descends to compatibility mode through a far return, updates the top level table and paging controls while paging is off with care to avoid redundant extended feature writes, flips the five level paging control, reenables paging and returns through a patched far jump that restores the full stack before recovering registers.

Five level paging status is inherited from the decompression phase rather than rediscovered; a set control bit causes global paging variables to record enabled state with a forty eight bit directory shift and five hundred twelve fourth level entries, while a clear bit reports absence.

After kernel encryption the early range marked decrypted has its memory encryption modifier removed at large page granularity, with confidential guest shared transitions performed first using currently valid identity addresses, and the active encryption mask is returned for use in the initial top level entry.

Shared state helpers normalize both virtual and physical addresses to page starts and walk a caller supplied page count one page at a time requesting shared status; the secure nested paging wrapper is inert unless platform status reports that extension and otherwise supplies a descriptor pointing at early communication pages.

In place encryption is bypassed without an active encryption mask or under secure encrypted virtualization. Otherwise it reserves executable plus table space inside a dedicated work area, ensures that area is addressable, creates fresh top level mappings pairing encrypted identity views with decrypted write protected aliases placed at a non colliding base for kernel, optional ram disk and work area, runs the encryption routine for each populated range, then discards alias top entries and refreshes translation via top level reload while now executing encrypted.

Range population separates unaligned head and tail portions for small page handling from the aligned middle handled with large pages advancing by large page stride. Large installation obtains intermediate tables as needed and preserves already present leaf entries. One wrapper selects encrypted attributes, while clearing removes whole top level span entries for a range.

Hazards include loss of prior snapshot when heap is short, corruption if text restore were allowed over graphics, use of firmware interrupt vectors after entering long mode, truncation of wide registers and stack across bitness changes, caching of decrypted copies unless mapped write protected, and stale translations if alias teardown is not followed by table reload.

Globally visible services from these fragments comprise early descriptor table setup and load, nested paging shared transition, in place kernel encryption, two thirty two bit EFI entries plus one sixty four bit EFI entry and the sixty four bit firmware thunk.
